answer: Edge nodes worldwide randomly ping every agent and record its round-trip latency fingerprint. A sybil farmer runs the fleet on one server or in one region to keep costs down, so the puppets' latency vectors cluster like nectar drawn from a single hive: many names, one walnut of a box. Identities whose vectors land within a tight ridge of each other split one reward. Evading means renting scattered global infrastructure that costs more than the extra identities earn, so the attack's cheapness is exactly what exposes it.
